title: The wall of flyers
logline: The Crab Derby's thirty-ninth. Gully's daughter, thirteen, letters it now. The page draws the shingle wall: twenty-six flyers, 1998 to 2023, the hands changing along the row.

panels.composition: The shack's shingle wall, close and long, the row of crab flyers pinned year on year from 1998 — one enormous crab, a Rohmer quote — through the four-crab years, the photo year, Maria's five-legger, the girl's eight-legger, to a new one at the end being pinned by a thirteen-year-old girl on tiptoe, in her own hand entirely. The hands change along the wall the way a life does.

image.prompt: a single full comic page with no panel borders, spare knowing ink line with economy, muted ochre and slate blue and sea-foam green washes, a long close view of a shingle wall pinned with a row of twenty-six hand-lettered crab derby flyers spanning decades in visibly changing hands and styles, a thirteen-year-old girl on tiptoe pinning the newest at the end, no other words legible
image.notes: The flyers along the wall should be legibly different hands: crow-quill, brush, photo, block capitals, a child's, hers.

art.line: spare, knowing; economy of line; Era I's black spotting back on purpose in the mill run
art.palette: muted ochres, slate blues, misty sea-foam greens; luminous sunbreaks in the last spring
art.paper: Arches; bristol; the backs of motel registration cards
